## Step-by-step Integration by Parts

**First application:** Let u = 2x⁵, dv = sin(x)dx → du = 10x⁴dx, v = -cos(x)

$$-2x^5\cos(x) + \int 10x^4\cos(x)\,dx$$

**Second:** Let u = 10x⁴, dv = cos(x)dx → du = 40x³dx, v = sin(x)

$$-2x^5\cos(x) + 10x^4\sin(x) - \int 40x^3\sin(x)\,dx$$

**Third:** Let u = 40x³, dv = sin(x)dx → du = 120x²dx, v = -cos(x)

$$-2x^5\cos(x) + 10x^4\sin(x) + 40x^3\cos(x) - \int 120x^2\cos(x)\,dx$$

**Fourth:** Let u = 120x², dv = cos(x)dx → du = 240xdx, v = sin(x)

$$-2x^5\cos(x) + 10x^4\sin(x) + 40x^3\cos(x) - 120x^2\sin(x) + \int 240x\sin(x)\,dx$$

**Fifth:** Let u = 240x, dv = sin(x)dx → du = 240dx, v = -cos(x)

$$-2x^5\cos(x) + 10x^4\sin(x) + 40x^3\cos(x) - 120x^2\sin(x) - 240x\cos(x) + \int 240\cos(x)\,dx$$

**Final:** ∫ 240cos(x)dx = 240sin(x)

Differentiating the result, all intermediate terms cancel, leaving exactly **2x⁵sin(x)** ✓
